item.title: One ongoing frustration is the lack of effort I see being put towards near-term, achievable crash projects to do good with AI at a national scale, whe...
item.description:
One ongoing frustration is the lack of effort I see being put towards near-term, achievable crash projects to do good with AI at a national scale, whether those efforts are by the AI labs or by policymakers & NGOs.

Some obvious ideas to explore suggested by the data we have so far: universal tutoring to support classroom learning, second opinions on healthcare, financial literacy/scam avoidance, and making government services easy to access.

These are hard problems, and I know because over the past 20 years I have worked extensively on building tutoring and financial literacy programs, which were always limited by existing technology. Now, real gains are likely achievable with AI, which should be a big deal. Yes, you would want to do careful design and studies before rolling things out. And yes, those efforts might fail. But, if done right, national programs could lead to big gains in public good for seemingly intractable problems. And they don't require AIs beyond current models to pull off.

Erik is one of the economists who has been watching the impact of AI on the economy most closely, even before generative AI...
Erik Brynjolfsson: Evidence is growing that we’re turning the corner on productivity.

US productivity grew at a 3.6% annual rate this past quarter.

That’s more than double the 1.5% average from 2007-2019.

The new numbers put me further ahead for my bet with Bob Gordon about productivity growth in the 2020s. 💪

Here’s how far the US is now ahead of the CBO estimate at the start of the decade (before they knew about the pandemic or LLMs) courtesy of @jasonfurman’s

item.description:
The AI slopcomments are out-of-control on X but also remarkably easy to stop if the company wanted to?

I did a little experiment and found that combining as few as five comments and running them through Pangram is good enough to weed out the slop and not punish real humans.

This is a fantastic idea - a mass attempted replication of old findings of LLMs with new models. Much conventional wisdom is outdated.

Recent models no longer invent citations and both hallucination rates & stereotyping has dropped. But they are still sycophantic & lean left.
